newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN SUPPORT FOR INNOVATION "TOO CAUTIOUS".
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN SUPPORT FOR INNOVATION "TOO CAUTIOUS".

text.p: South African state support for technology development was too cautious and could be expanded to big business, an official of the department of trade and industry said on Wednesday.
Alan Hirsch, chief director in the DTI, told a parliamentary committee his department's Support Programme for Industrial Innovation had yet to fulfill its potential.
"It's a fairly conservative programme," he said.

"Our main concern has been that it hasn't been sufficiently well marketed. It has been too risk averse...The more risks you take, the more it will cost government but the more chance you will have of having spectacular successes," Hirsch said.
The programme provides matching grants to small and medium enterprises seeking to improve their manufacturing technologies.
Hirsch said the programme was being re-evaluated.

"It doesn't really meet the need of large companies developing large technology projects. We are looking at the possibility of a sister programme that will address their needs more effectively, probably on the basis of a loan," he said.
